name: Cedar Park
seo_title: Cedar Park Christmas Events for Kids 2026: 9 Events, 4 Free
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Cedar Park, TX: the Heritage Oak Tree Lighting, Sky Trail of Lights, Santa at SCHEELS, a Grinch storytime and H-E-B Center shows.
lede: Cedar Park starts the season under a glowing live oak at Heritage Oak Park, then spreads the cheer to a YMCA light trail, Santa visits, holiday concerts and big shows at the H-E-B Center.
celebrates: The City of Cedar Park lights its largest live oak tree at Heritage Oak Park on Quest Parkway, with holiday music and photos with Santa under the branches, and the park stays lit through December. Families walk the Sky Trail of Lights at the Twin Lakes Family YMCA and the free Trail of Cheer at The Fieldhouse at The Crossover. Santa visits SCHEELS, Paper Bark Birch hosts a storytime with the Grinch and Cindy Lou Who, and the H-E-B Center brings touring holiday shows. Lakeline Park adds Light Up Lakeline, a newer city evening.
lastyear: In 2025 the city held the Heritage Oak Tree Lighting on Wednesday, December 3, from 6:30 to 8:30 pm at Heritage Oak Park, 875 Quest Parkway. The city calendar promised more than 50,000 sparkling lights on Cedar Park's largest live oak, festive holiday music and photos with Santa beneath the tree. The city moved the lighting to a Wednesday that year to make room for its newest holiday event, A Jolly Bright Lakeline Night.
facts: Cedar Park was first called Running Brushy, after a strong spring that formed the headwaters of Brushy Creek. When the Austin and Northwestern Railroad arrived in 1882, the railroad renamed the stop Brueggerhoff. In 1887 Emmett Cluck renamed the town Cedar Park after the parklike land around his home. Limestone and cedar fence posts were the town's big products for decades, and residents voted to incorporate on February 24, 1973.
trains: Cedar Park grew up beside the Austin and Northwestern Railroad, finished from Austin to Burnet in 1882. Today the same corridor carries the CapMetro Red Line, whose Lakeline station is the stop for Cedar Park, one stop before the end of the line in Leander. The Austin Steam Train Association runs the Hill Country Flyer from Cedar Park to Burnet and the North Pole Flyer from its 1912 Bertram Depot, with unlimited hot chocolate. The closest Amtrak stations are Austin, Taylor and San Marcos on the Texas Eagle.

traditions: The city lights its largest live oak at Heritage Oak Park with holiday music and photos with Santa.
The park on Quest Parkway glows with thousands of lights all through December.
The Twin Lakes Family YMCA turns its grounds into a walk through light trail, with an optional ropes course ride.
The Fieldhouse at The Crossover sets up a free holiday walk through.
A newer city evening of lights and holiday fun at Lakeline Park.
kidfact: Long ago Cedar Park was called Running Brushy, named for a bubbling spring that starts Brushy Creek. The town got its new name in 1887 because the land looked like a park full of cedar trees.
faq: Where is the Cedar Park Christmas tree lighting?

The City of Cedar Park lights the Heritage Oak at Heritage Oak Park, 875 Quest Parkway, Cedar Park, TX 78613. It is the city's largest live oak, and the city wraps it in tens of thousands of lights. The evening includes holiday music and photos with Santa under the tree, and the park stays lit for the rest of December.
Where can kids see Christmas lights in Cedar Park?

Heritage Oak Park on Quest Parkway is lit through December. The Twin Lakes Family YMCA runs the Sky Trail of Lights, where walking the lights is free and the Sky Trail ropes course ride costs extra. The Fieldhouse at The Crossover hosts the free Trail of Cheer walk through, and the city adds Light Up Lakeline at Lakeline Park.
Is there a Christmas train near Cedar Park?

Yes. The Austin Steam Train Association is based in Cedar Park and runs the North Pole Flyer from its 1912 Bertram Depot, with unlimited hot chocolate on board. Its Hill Country Flyer runs from Cedar Park to Burnet. The CapMetro Red Line stops at Lakeline station, so kids can also ride a commuter train into downtown Austin.
Where can kids meet Santa in Cedar Park?

Santa poses for photos at the Heritage Oak Tree Lighting, and the city also hosts Breakfast with Santa and Photos with Santa evenings. SCHEELS Cedar Park holds a free Meet Santa day in its store. Check each host's page for the current dates, because city programs often need registration and some sessions sell out.
How did Cedar Park get its name?

The Texas State Historical Association says the community began as Running Brushy, then the railroad renamed it Brueggerhoff in 1882. In 1887 Emmett Cluck renamed it Cedar Park after the parklike setting of his home. Limestone and cedar posts were major products for decades, and the city incorporated in 1973.
